newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov wants pay raises linked to on-time budget.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov wants pay raises linked to on-time budget.

text.p: New York Gov George Pataki, who last year set a national record for late budgets, proposed to legislative leaders that he would back a pay increase for them in return for a budget passed on time, legislative sources said Monday.
Spokesmen for Pataki, Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, and Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, either had no comment or were not immediately available.
The legislative sources declined to be named.
Any pay increase, sure to be controversial with voters, would not help sitting legislators, however, as by state law, they cannot raise their own salaries.
Instead, the first legislature that would get any rise in pay, which would boost base salaries to as much as $75,000 a year from $57,000, would be the 1999 state Assembly and Senate.

Albany lawmakers have grown frustrated over the past several years, when they have gone without pay rises only to see other elected officials, like New York City Council members, who earn $70,500 a year, eclipse their base pay.
This has increased the importance of stipends, which last December were the subject of a bruising battle between the Assembly Democrats and Pataki.
New York State, whose budgets are due on April 1, failed to approve its 1997 fiscal budget until 104 days past the deadline--and this was the 12th pact in a row to be late.
